name: Malawi

findings.local_actor: Government of Malawi; Electricity Supply Corporation of Malawi (ESCOM)
findings.summary: Phase II of Malawi's National Fibre Backbone, launched June 2021 and implemented by Huawei, covers nearly 3,000 km of fibre; AidData records a China Eximbank concessional loan (signed August 2020) financing it, on-lent to ESCOM.

sources.publisher: AidData (William & Mary) Chinese development finance dataset

findings.analyst_inference: Equipment vendor Huawei sets the pole. Tier 4 = loan signed and construction launched; completion not confirmed. AidData (research dataset, treated as S2) gives RMB 693m, World Bank DRS face value about US$100.5m, disbursed RMB 299m by June 2023 amid Malawi debt-distress rescheduling talks; value fields left null because this is the loan, not a verified project award. Phase I (2017-18, 28 districts, about $23m) was also Huawei-built with ESCOM per Developing Telecoms. Audit 2026-10-28: AidData: RMB 299.3m disbursed by June 2023; rescheduling unresolved July 2023; Phase II completion not confirmed.

findings.summary: Malawi's first National Data Centre, in Blantyre, was launched in July 2022 to host government-wide systems; it was built by Huawei as part of the National Fibre Backbone project.

sources.publisher: AidData (William & Mary) Chinese development finance dataset

findings.analyst_inference: Owner-operator is the Malawian government, so the pole is domestic; Huawei is builder and China Eximbank the financier (Phase II loan per AidData). The IT equipment inside is likely Huawei but no source names it, so no silicon/IT finding is coded. The 2026 PPPC item describes Blantyre as the disaster-recovery site for the new Lilongwe centre; this role assignment is inferred from that article.

findings.local_actor: Ministry of ICT / Public Private Partnership Commission
findings.summary: A World Bank-funded National Data Centre in Lilongwe, begun under the Digital Malawi Foundation Project, was reported fully completed in April 2026, already hosting eleven government systems and six co-locating ministries, linked to the Blantyre site.

sources.publisher: Public Private Partnership Commission, Digital Malawi Acceleration Project
Public Private Partnership Commission, Digital Malawi Acceleration Project

findings.analyst_inference: Single S1 host (both items are PPPC pages). Contractor and IT equipment vendor not named. A World Bank IDA-funded expansion (RFB MW-PPPC-494042-GO-RFB) was at early-market-engagement stage in October 2025; no award found, so not coded separately. Tier 5 reflects reported operational hosting, at modest scale.

findings.summary: TNM switched on Malawi's first 5G pilot sites in Blantyre and Lilongwe in May 2023 with Huawei as rollout partner, after a roughly US$5m, two-year packet-core modernisation.
findings.analyst_inference: Pilot = tier 2. Developing Telecoms says the MWK5.2bn (US$5m) investment was made with Huawei, implying a Huawei packet core, but whether Huawei supplied core as well as RAN is not stated explicitly. DCD (Nov 2025) reports TNM went commercially live with 5G around July 2025; the vendor for that launch was not confirmed. Value not entered because the $5m is not clearly a Huawei contract value.

findings.summary: TNM's CEO described a close relationship with Huawei as a major supplier, said TNM should not be wholly dependent on it, and its 2014 US$20m deferred-payment facility with Huawei covered equipment purchases.
findings.analyst_inference: Article undated; context (2018 annual report, US-Huawei row) suggests 2019. Pre-2020; the 2023 Huawei 5G pilot suggests the relationship continued but still_current is not confirmed. Article wording calls Huawei a 'client', read here as supplier. US$20m facility is a financing line, not a verified contract value, so value fields are null.

findings.local_actor: StarLink Lilongwe Ltd; Malawi Communications Regulatory Authority (MACRA)
findings.summary: MACRA issued SpaceX's local subsidiary network facilities, network services and application service licences, the first satellite broadband licence of its kind in Malawi, pending gazetting and spectrum assignment.
findings.analyst_inference: Licence issued = tier 4. Single opened source. Satellite access network, controlled by the US operator. Audit 2026-10-28: An unopened search result reports Starlink's later commercial launch in Malawi.

findings.reversal_of: Starlink new-subscription sales under the 2022 MACRA licence (MWI-006)
findings.summary: Starlink suspended new residential and most business subscriptions in Malawi after MACRA rejected a price increase meant to offset the kwacha's devaluation; existing subscribers were not affected.
findings.analyst_inference: Partial pause, not an exit. Coded commercial: the suspension was Starlink's response to pricing and foreign-exchange constraints, not a security or alignment decision, though a regulator's price ruling triggered it. Whether new sales have resumed was not checked. Audit 2026-10-28: Coding a temporary sales pause as a tier-4 reversal is an analytic choice the source does not settle; whether sales resumed was not checked.

findings.controller: Government of Malawi (Malawi Low Resource Language Data Trust Initiative)
findings.summary: Malawi's government launched a Chichewa AI initiative through a national language data trust, backed by the World Bank and Gates Foundation, to assemble licensed Chichewa content and core AI frameworks for local-language tools.
findings.analyst_inference: A data and capability initiative, not yet a model; no base model or model provider named, so base_model is null. Coded domestic on the expectation that the data trust is nationally controlled; tier 1 because only a launch and intentions are reported.

silicon.null_reason: search budget spent on networks, facilities, models and applications; no accelerator purchases or export licences surfaced incidentally

applications.null_reason: two searches found an IDS report saying Malawi spent over $27m on interception and biometric-ID contracts with US, UK, Chinese, EU and Israeli firms, but no vendor named; China's 2021 police donation was non-digital gear; no safe-city contract found

power.null_reason: no AI- or data-centre-specific power evidence surfaced

corrections.note: Source-verified corrections and audit notes: MWI-002, MWI-003, MWI-001, MWI-006, MWI-007

research_gaps: Which vendor supplied Airtel Malawi's 5G (56 sites, Nov 2025) and its RAN/core generally? DCD says the vendor is unknown.
Which vendor supported TNM's commercial 5G launch (~July 2025), and is Huawei TNM's core as well as RAN supplier today?
Status of National Fibre Backbone Phase II (Huawei, China Eximbank loan): completed? Outcome of the Malawi-China Eximbank rescheduling talks?
Who won the World Bank-funded National Data Centre expansion (RFB MW-PPPC-494042-GO-RFB), and which IT vendors equip the Lilongwe and Blantyre centres?
Vendor names behind Malawi's ~$27m interception and biometric-ID surveillance contracts (IDS 'Mapping the Supply of Surveillance Technologies to Africa' report).
Has Starlink resumed new subscriptions in Malawi since the October 2024 suspension?
WAICO status is unconfirmed in the global layer (single S3 roster); confirm or deny.
